section: 16. Escape from the Evil God: Return to Modern Times
description: The evil god manifests, everyone runs frantically, escaping the ancient time-space at the last moment, consciousness returns to the Orient Express

conversation.speaker: player9
conversation.text: "Even fly meat is still meat, three silver coins will do, let's take them back to melt first." #Calling these two to the military camp furnace to dissolve them.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "If you ask me—to hell with the dragon!" The poet tugged at his collar to fan himself, "We've been through all this trouble, enough to write three biographies of Saint George, and all we get is a lousy coin? Ironclad Lord, you might as well use that money to get some clues about the armor! Anyway, that dragon won't leave the reservoir. After we kill Sadi Fikar, we can deal with it later."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "So, should we go report to the Count?"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Pack up and go report to the Count.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Everyone stepped into the Count's fortress. The air was filled with a mix of incense and leather. Count Baldwin was leaning over an oak table, his fingers tapping impatiently on a spread-out map of Constantinople.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Present the scroll.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The Count narrowed his eyes, his fingers hovering above the scroll. "So... the whereabouts of Sadi Fikar?"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "The old leper gave us guidance. The faceless one is hard to uncover, but ultimately cannot escape this method."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The poet lowered his voice. "According to that bandaged lord, the simulacrum and the original are like a spider and its web—find one, and the other is nearby." He glanced at the scroll. "As for the specific location... it depends on whether you're willing to sponsor some 'investigation funds'?" Suddenly, he showed a sly smile.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "We still lack a piece of human skin."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "A bowl of water, snake scales, a raven's black feather, rotten wax, and a piece of living human skin."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Considering how many people are not worth living nowadays."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "We only need living human skin now."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Of course!" The poet quickly added. "Such rough work can be left to those Venetian spies in the dungeon—they're going to the gallows sooner or later anyway, might as well make use of them!"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "This isn't a difficult material."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Skinning? Do it in the dungeon." He looked up, scanning everyone with a gaze sharp as a knife. "Anyway, those Venetian rats are going to die sooner or later. Might as well make use of them while they're still alive."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "As you command, my Lord."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The Count took a black iron token from his waist and threw it on the table. "Show this to the executioner in the dungeon." The corner of his mouth twisted into a cold smile. "As for the prisoner... pick one who doesn't scream much. Last time, the screams made me lose a chess game."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Thank you for your assistance."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Also, if the location revealed in the water is the palace or a church, report to me first. Don't act on your own."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Yes, my Lord."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Prepare to leave the Count's place to go kill a prisoner.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Go to the dungeon.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The entrance to the dungeon was hidden under a half-collapsed Byzantine stone tower behind the military camp. The narrow spiral staircase emitted a foul smell of mold and rotten blood. With each step down, the air grew thicker. The poet held a torch to illuminate the dungeon. The main part of the dungeon was a vaulted stone cave, the walls covered with dried bloody handprints. Five iron cages hung above a sewage pool, holding several prisoners who were barely human. In the corner, a charcoal brazier held several red-hot branding irons. The so-called "executioner" was a one-eyed Serbian giant, carving what looked like a piece of dried human ear with a dagger.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "God needs you, my child."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Show the token.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: When player6 showed the token, the executioner's one eye gleamed. "Hmm, which one?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Hmm... do you have a bigger one?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Venetian liar? Genoese pirate? Or this Greek brat who stole the communion wafer? Fresh!" He finally pointed at the smallest cage.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "One with intact skin."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: He slowly stood up, twirling the dagger in his palm, then pointed towards the depths of the dungeon. "You want a big one?" He grinned, revealing several uneven yellow teeth. "There's a Byzantine rebel deserter locked up further back, muscles like an ox, and his voice is particularly loud!"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Let's save him, we'll take a look first."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: He led everyone through the damp passageway. Behind the iron bars of the innermost cell, a giant man was curled up, his hands and feet shackled with iron chains, his bare back covered in whip marks and unhealed branding scars. Hearing the noise, he jerked his head up, his turbid eyes filled with a mix of fear and anger.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Is having a brand okay?"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Let's pick a quieter one."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The poet took a quick step closer to the iron bars, carefully examining the giant man by torchlight. Suddenly, he turned his head with a sly smile and pointed at the intact skin on the giant man's side. "Oh! Look at this luck!"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Him it is."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The executioner grinned, pulling out a rusty key and jamming it into the lock. The iron bars let out a teeth-grating groan before opening.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Whisper "Remember to knock him out. The Count doesn't like noise."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The executioner stepped forward cooperatively and pressed on the giant man's neck.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Turns head away.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Grabs the dagger, then waits for the strong man to not react and gives his head a whack with the club to knock him out.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Can't bear to watch, leaves first.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Then starts cutting the skin from the strong man's back, hands the club to the jailer, gesturing to give him another whack if he wakes up from the pain.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You deftly cut out the skin of the required size.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Not as profound as what my colleague did to the parish boys."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The poet choked violently, then burst into exaggerated laughter, almost dropping the torch into the sewage ditch.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Gathers all the materials, feeling the maid lady is less willing to touch them.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Is everything ready? Let's go perform the ritual."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Find a quiet place and perform the ritual according to the method.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Faith arises from desire. If it is what you hope for, it will surely receive a response. <player7>'s 75 Wish:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: (Natural History is not allowed.)

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Stretches. "Looks like my skills are lacking. Gotta go find Old Leper."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player7 placed the flayed skin into a copper bowl filled with water, sprinkled in snake scales, black feathers, and rotten wax, and softly chanted the incantation from the scroll. The water surface initially rippled, as if something was about to appear—then with a "poof," it went out.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "I'm more inclined to think Jesus is messing with us." #Shrugs.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then you obtain another piece.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Let's go find Old Leper. Speaking of which, I haven't run into that old bastard for a while."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Let's go."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Run off to find Old Leper.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then everyone arrives at the ship. The poet kicked aside the fishing nets piled on the deck of the Plague Rat. The lepers shrank back into the shadows like startled cockroaches. "Bandage Lord! Emergency aid!" He dragged player7 forward and slapped the bloody second piece of skin into the bandaged hand of Brother Melovac. "Your ritual translation must have missed something. Our own attempt at the ritual failed!"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Actually, I've done too many wicked things and have been cursed by Jesus (Qiduo)."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The monk silently took the skin, then immersed the second piece into the copper bowl containing other materials. The water suddenly boiled, revealing a blurry image—a crimson tower. "North side, Golden Horn Bay." The monk uttered a hoarse voice.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Thank you. So our next step is to go there?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Yes."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Thanks, old chap."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Next stop—the Crimson Sightseeing Tower!" The poet stood with one foot on the gunwale, pointing towards the faintly visible scarlet tower on the north shore.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Shouldn't we gather some more manpower?"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Let's go to the square to recruit some mercenaries."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Agreed. We can't let a tragedy like last time happen again."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Ha! Monk, your 'fear of insufficient combat power' is a lingering effect from being chased by the dragon last time, isn't it?"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Try to recruit some reliable ones. We should declare we are under the Earl's command."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "You jest, my lord. Those two were practically bedridden for a whole day after returning."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Hehe, let's send the mercenaries in first—wait until they and the cultists have stabbed each other enough, then 'settle accounts' with the survivor!"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "In short, if we face that dragon again, it's likely to be more perilous than not."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I think that makes a lot of sense."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #touches his own charred skin

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "But it seems a bit difficult to pull off."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "If I ever become a saint, I'll definitely be the patron saint of the burned and impaled."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Difficulty? Let me calculate—" The poet cleared his throat with great ceremony. "Step one: Throw a torch at the Crimson Tower, pretending it's dragon fire! Step two: Throw cultist items into the reservoir, pretending it's a provocation from the cultists!"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Plan successful! Let's do it!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Don't worry!" Hearing the monk's words, the poet patted his back. "If we fail, we can still pretend to be innocent bystanders." He pulled out a grimy white cloth and tied it to player7's staff. "Look! A makeshift surrender flag, all prepared!"

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "Or poison."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "So, who throws the torch, and who throws the cultist stuff?" The poet asked, pumped with adrenaline.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I can go throw the cultist items."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Then I'll throw the torch, and the rest of you get ready to clean up the aftermath!" The poet volunteered.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Should I go alone?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: At the Crimson Tower side, the poet pulled a torch from his robe, rubbed it twice against a rope soaked in fish oil, and flames whooshed up. He squinted, aiming at the top of the crimson tower, swung his arm in a full circle, "Off you go!" The torch spun through the night sky, its flames madly climbing the wooden scaffolding on the tower's exterior, instantly wrapping the entire tower into a giant torch. The poet stepped back to admire his handiwork. "Aha! This heat—"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: .ra Stealth 85

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: @player4

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Faith arises from desire. What you hope for will surely receive a response. <player6>'s Stealth 85 Wish:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player6 silently slips into the shadows at the edge of the reservoir. The water's surface is as calm as a piece of dark green glass, reflecting the night sky. The dragon's massive silhouette looms faintly beneath the water, like a slowly unfurling piece of volcanic rock—its thick tail occasionally sweeps across the pool bottom, stirring up a string of pearl-like bubbles before quickly settling back into silence.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Carefully peeking out

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The dragon is faintly visible in the water and hasn't noticed you.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Taking out that "Do Not Open" box from inside my coat

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player6 seizes the moment the dragon raises its head to look at the sky, flicks their wrist, and the box arcs into the water. As the box sinks, the dragon's jaws snap open, its sharp teeth precisely biting the box—a cracking sound amplified tenfold by the water's surface, and a crimson, slimy membrane like a living creature shoots out, instantly wrapping around the dragon's upper jaw. The membrane sizzles like frying lard, rapidly corroding down to bare bone.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Holy shit

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The Crimson Tower, fueled by dragonfire, begins to burn even more fiercely, bricks cracking, thick smoke billowing. Sedefikar appears at the tower's peak, black robes fluttering, a cold light gleaming from the blade in his hand. Simultaneously, three skin demons crawl from the shadows at the tower's base, stitched together from countless human skins, dark red flames flickering in their empty eye sockets, silently pouncing towards the dragon.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Staring dumbfounded

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The body covered in stitch marks springs up at an unnatural angle, the flaying blade carving a deadly arc. As dragon teeth pierce the cultist's chest, the blade also slices open the dragon's throat artery. Scalding dragon blood and foul bodily fluids pour down like a rainstorm onto the dock's stone pavement, mixing into a boiling, purplish-black mire.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Eh... another sanity check? I understand, everyone's watching.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "My God..." #Kneeling down to start praying

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Eh... another sanity check? I understand, everyone's watching.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The dying dragon's foreclaw is embedded between Sedefikar's ribs, while the cultist's blade is lodged in the dragon's cervical vertebrae. The light in their pupils flickers like dying embers amidst their fading gasps.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Eh... another sanity check? I understand, everyone's watching.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Eh... another sanity check? I understand, everyone's watching.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Pinned to the ground by the dragon's claw, chest shattered, black blood gushing, Sedefikar's fingers still claw desperately into the dirt, dragging his broken body forward inch by inch. Deep within the tower's ruins, an eerie blue-green light seeps from a crack in the shattered altar, writhing like a living thing, as if calling to him. He rasps out an incantation, using his blade stuck in the ground for support. The dragon's breath is faint, but it still struggles in its death throes, its claws unconsciously tightening, almost cutting the cultist in half. But Sedefikar laughs maniacally, his withered fingertips finally about to touch the edge of the light—instantly, his skin begins to dissolve, bones twisting and deforming, as if being reshaped by some indescribable force. The blue-green light spreads like a tide along his arm, pulling him bit by bit towards the altar's center, his mad laughter gradually turning into an inhuman shriek, like a million human skins wailing at once.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #The club quietly taps the ground ("Ha, serves you right for blasting me so enthusiastically")

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The poet in the distance suddenly stands up, face paling. "Damn it! This lunatic is about to summon the real thing!"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Huh? What's that?
